answer: To resist sybils, an agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake in a kernel registry to trade. Creating one fake identity is cheap, but running a voyage of hundreds means locking capital per identity, and the stake is slashed if peers prove duplicate behavior. A zephyr of free accounts cannot outvote bonded ones because voting weight scales with locked stake and earned attestations, not headcount. The attacker's cost grows linearly with every fake, while honest agents reuse one bonded identity across many deals, so forgery stays unprofitable.
